scenario.title: 到維修中心描述手機問題
scenario.context: 「我的手機壞了」「螢幕被摔破了」「它被送去原廠」——講東西壞掉時，英文要分清楚是「它自己壞了」還是「被弄壞了」。這是被動語態最自然的入門場景。

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.en: Hi, what seems to be the problem?

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: My phone won't turn on. It just died yesterday afternoon.
lines.zh: 我手機開不了機，昨天下午突然就掛了。

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.en: Did you drop it or get it wet?

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: No, nothing like that. It was updating, and then the screen went black.
lines.zh: 沒有。它在更新，然後螢幕就黑了。

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.en: Sounds like it got bricked during the update. Let me run a quick test.
lines.zh: 聽起來像是更新時變磚了，我先幫你簡單測試。

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.en: Yeah, the software's corrupted. It needs to be sent to the main service center.
lines.zh: 對，軟體損毀了，需要送回總維修中心。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: How long will that take? And will my photos be deleted?
lines.zh: 要多久？我的照片會被刪掉嗎？

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.en: About a week. And unfortunately, the data might be wiped. Is it backed up?
lines.zh: 大概一週。很遺憾資料可能會被清空。你有備份嗎？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I think it was backed up to the cloud last week. Fingers crossed.
lines.zh: 我記得上週有備份到雲端。祈禱一下。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Wait, didn't you just get that phone?
lines.zh: 等等，你那支手機不是才剛買嗎？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Eight months ago. And this is the second time it's been repaired.
lines.zh: 八個月前。而且這是第二次送修了。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Sounds like you got a lemon.
lines.zh: 聽起來你買到瑕疵品了。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Totally. The first time, the screen was replaced because of dead pixels.
lines.zh: 完全是。第一次是因為壞點，換了螢幕。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Can you ask for a new one? It's still under warranty, right?
lines.zh: 你可以要求換新嗎？還在保固內對吧？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Yeah, I'm going to ask. Meanwhile I'm using my old phone, which is on its last legs.
lines.zh: 對，我會問。這段期間我先用舊手機，它也快不行了。

patterns.note: won't = 就是不肯，形容東西不運作很傳神

patterns.en: How long will the repair take?
How much will it cost to fix?

chinglish.wrong: My phone is broken by itself.
chinglish.right: My phone just stopped working. / My phone broke.
chinglish.why: is broken by itself 混合了被動和「自己」，邏輯打架。東西自己壞掉就用主動的 broke / stopped working / died。

chinglish.right: My phone broke. / My phone was broken.
chinglish.why: 被動要 be + 過去分詞（broken），broke 是過去式。另外 broke 當形容詞是「沒錢」，I'm broke = 我沒錢。

chinglish.right: The phone needs to be repaired. / The phone needs repairing.
chinglish.why: 手機是「被修」的，要用被動 to be repaired。

chinglish.right: My phone froze. / My phone keeps freezing.
chinglish.why: 「當機」直翻成 dead machine 不是英文。當機是 freeze / crash。

grammar.title: 被動入門：broke vs was broken
grammar.oneLiner: 主詞「自己做」用主動；主詞「被做」用被動 be + p.p.。重點不在誰做的時候，就用被動。
whenToUse: 被動 = be + 過去分詞：was replaced, is being repaired, will be sent, has been fixed。
用被動的時機：不知道是誰做的、誰做的不重要，或重點是「東西」而不是「人」。The screen was replaced.
有些動詞主動就能表示「自己發生」：The phone broke. / The screen cracked. / The glass broke.
The phone broke（它壞了，發生的事件）vs The phone is broken（它現在是壞的，描述狀態）。
真的要說是誰做的，才加 by：It was repaired by a technician.
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 中文的被動常靠「被」字，但日常很少用：「手機送修了」「螢幕換好了」其實都是被動意思，卻沒有「被」。台灣人不習慣判斷主詞是主動還是被動，所以會寫出 The phone needs to repair（手機需要去修理別人）或 The screen replaced（螢幕去替換了什麼）。

examples.correct: The screen was replaced last month.
examples.note: 螢幕是被換的，要用被動。
東西自己壞了，主動就可以。

examples.correct: Your phone will be sent to the service center.

examples.note: It needs to charge 口語其實也聽得到，但指的是「需要充電」這件事；正式寫法用被動。

quiz.question: My phone screen ___ last week. It looks brand new now.
Oh no, the glass ___! Who put it on the edge?
quiz.explanation: 東西自己破了，用主動的過去式。

quiz.question: Your laptop will be ___ (fix) by Friday.
This printer needs ___.
quiz.explanation: 印表機是被修理的，用被動。

quiz.question: All my photos ___ backed up to the cloud yesterday. (were / was)
quiz.explanation: photos 是複數，過去被動用 were + p.p.。

slang.meaning: （電子產品）變磚、完全無法開機
slang.usage: 裝置壞到跟磚頭一樣沒用，常用在更新失敗後。brick 也可以當動詞。

risk.note: 科技圈常用語，一般人也懂。

examples.zh: 更新讓我的平板變磚了。

examples.en: Don't unplug it during the update or it might get bricked.
examples.zh: 更新時別拔插頭，不然可能會變磚。

slang.meaning: 瑕疵品、問題很多的產品（特別是車）
slang.usage: 買到一直出問題的東西：I got a lemon. 美國甚至有 Lemon Law（瑕疵車保護法）。

examples.en: My first car was a lemon. It broke down every month.
examples.zh: 我第一台車是爛車，每個月都拋錨。

examples.en: If it breaks again, it's definitely a lemon.
examples.zh: 如果再壞，那絕對是瑕疵品。

slang.usage: My phone's dead = 我手機沒電了。也可以說機器完全壞了。

risk.note: 日常最常用的說法之一。

examples.en: Sorry I didn't reply. My phone was dead.
examples.zh: 抱歉沒回你，我手機沒電了。

examples.en: Can I borrow your charger? My battery's almost dead.
examples.zh: 可以借你的充電器嗎？我快沒電了。

slang.usage: 形容東西很舊快壞了；用在人（on his last legs）則是很累或快撐不住。

risk.note: 講物品很安全；講人時注意語境，可能暗示病重。

examples.en: My laptop is on its last legs. It takes ten minutes to start.
examples.zh: 我的筆電快掛了，開機要十分鐘。

examples.en: This washing machine is on its last legs.

review.question: You look exhausted. You ___ go home early.
review.explanation: 複習第 17 單元：一般建議用 should + 原形。

review.question: I'm going to call in ___ today. I can't stop coughing.
review.explanation: 複習第 17 單元：call in sick。

review.question: Which is most natural?
review.explanation: 複習第 16 單元：人的所有物用 's。

review.question: Do you mind ___ (wait) a few minutes?
The party is ___, so bring your own drinks.
review.explanation: 複習第 10 單元：BYOB = 酒水自備。

review.question: Which is the most polite way to order?
options: Could I have a sandwich, please?
review.explanation: 複習第 2 單元：Could I have… please?

review.question: My phone ___ so I couldn't call you. (沒電了)
review.explanation: My phone was dead = 手機沒電了。
